analysis.title: 10/30 Mkt Internal Insight: Excess Flow & Systematic Rebalance Intraday Update II
key_insights: Systematic funds are estimated to sell $70-120 bn on 10/30 across Risk Control, Leveraged ETFs and CTA. Risk Control may sell up to $150 bn next Monday, depending on the final SPX return for the day.

Excess flow was -$89 bn of excess sell flow for the S&P 500 with SPY -2.3%, and -$50 bn for the Nasdaq 100 with QQQ -4.2%. The selling footprint was steady through the afternoon, which UBS reads as systematic selling.

UBS RMM clients turned to a modest sell-the-dip with flow almost flat at the 41st percentile vs 3Y. They sold tech stocks (software and IT services), selectively bought hardware and bought tech ETFs (QQQ, SOX and their leveraged ETFs).
UBS attributes the offset between tech ETF buying and tech stock selling by RMM clients potentially to year-end tax-loss harvesting.

With SPX -2.2%, Risk Control is estimated to sell $165-220 bn: $55-70 bn on 10/30 and $110-150 bn next Monday, with possible spillover to Tuesday. This is the first meaningful 1-day Risk Control rebalance since Nov 2025.
Prior large 1-day Risk Control unwinds were seen on Feb 8 2018, Aug 6 2019, Jul 2024, Dec 2024, Apr 2025, Oct 2025 and Nov 2025.
Leveraged ETFs are poised to sell $35 bn with QQQ -4.0%, of which $31 bn is in QQQ and tech: $16.8 bn semis, $10.1 bn QQQ, $0.6 bn MAG-7 and $3.4 bn other tech.

CTA equity sell triggers were crossed in ES1 (5 triggers), NQ1 (4 triggers) and RTY1 (1 trigger). The next ES1 trigger is at 7556.5 (-0.2%), the next NQ1 triggers are at 28036 (-0.9%) plus a moving average crossover within 4 days, and the next RTY1 triggers are at 2735.5 and 2716.9.
VIX at 23.5 puts the VIX Cross-Asset Rank at 85%, which UBS calls high but not stretched.

The sell-off triggered more pension month-end global equity buying than previously estimated: +$46 bn of global equity to buy ($12 bn US, $34 bn international) against global bonds to sell. It is the largest pension dollar buying since June 2022, and the largest in % of SPX market cap since March 2020 after adjusting for SPX returns.
risk_factors: Risk Control selling of up to $150 bn next Monday could spill over to Tuesday, depending on the final SPX return.
Leveraged ETF selling is concentrated in semis and QQQ, which adds pressure to those names.
Further CTA sell triggers are close in ES1 (-0.2%) and NQ1 (-0.9% plus a moving average crossover within 4 days).

Risk Control sensitivity grid: -1% = $15-25 bn to sell ($5-10 bn today, $10-15 bn tomorrow); -1.5% = $65-100 bn; -2% = $135-180 bn; -2.5% = $200-280 bn; -3.0% = $270-360 bn ($70-85 bn today, $200-275 bn tomorrow).
CTA equity exposure percentiles vs 3Y: ES1 at 18th, NQ1 at 13th, RTY1 at 15th.
Top 10 leveraged ETF stocks to sell in dollars: NVDA, AMD, MU, AVGO, INTC, AAPL, MSFT, TXN, ADI, QCOM.
Top 10 leveraged ETF stocks to sell as % of ADV: NXPI, ADI, MPWR, MCHP, TXN, QCOM, KLAC, TER, ON, ALAB.
VIX at 23.5 with a VIX Cross-Asset Rank of 85%, described as high but not stretched.
Pension month-end rebalance estimated at +$46 bn global equity buying, offsetting part of the systematic selling.

tension_points.bull_case: Pension month-end rebalancing adds an estimated +$46 bn of global equity buying ($12 bn US, $34 bn international), the largest in dollars since June 2022. VIX Cross-Asset Rank at 85% is high but not stretched.
tension_points.bear_case: Systematic funds are estimated to sell $70-120 bn on 10/30, and Risk Control may sell up to $150 bn next Monday. Leveraged ETFs add $35 bn of selling, concentrated in semis and QQQ.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The Risk Control selling estimate depends on the final SPX return on 10/30. At -1% the total falls to $15-25 bn, while at -3.0% it rises to $270-360 bn.
